description: Clock divider counting incoming pulses 1 to 8 over and over, with a CV input that sets how far the eight divisions are shifted round the eight output jacks

inputs.text: Each rise past 1.7V advances the count; the first pulse after a reset only measures the interval, and counting starts on the one after it
The voltage here, rounded to the nearest volt and reduced by one, shifts the divisions 0 to 7 jacks down; 0V and 1V leave them unshifted, 1.5V moves them one jack, and 8V or more moves them seven
A rise past 1.7V sets the count back to the start; the next pulse after it measures the interval and counting resumes on the one after that; it leaves the shift where it is

outputs.text: Unshifted, goes high on each count that divides by its own number, carrying the CLOCK input's own voltage rather than the 1.7V the manual states; SHFT moves which division arrives here

notes: an output that has gone high falls again after half the last measured clock interval, so the pulse width follows the incoming clock
nothing comes out until a clock is patched to CLOCK, and the first pulse after the module is added or reset only measures the interval, so the outputs start on the second pulse
the lamp beside an output is lit while that output is high
the count is not written into the patch file, so it starts from the beginning each time the patch is loaded
